plan.expected_behavior: The median ensemble suppresses extreme continuation estimates, while out-of-fold policy construction prevents optimistic reuse of fitted paths. Positive-payoff filtering concentrates capacity where exercise is feasible. Buffer calibration directly targets the primal objective and should improve both the high-volatility out-of-the-money put and correlated max-call lower bounds, with fewer low-margin premature exercises and lower seed sensitivity than the parent.
plan.failure_condition: Reject the intervention if matched-seed evaluation shows a negative mean discounted-payoff difference versus the unchanged parent, or if improvement disappears when buffer selection is evaluated strictly out of fold. Also fail safe to a strongly regularized linear model when an exercise date has fewer than 24 positive-payoff samples.
plan.implementation: Run backward induction with 4 deterministic folds. At each exercise date, fit continuation only on paths with positive immediate payoff, using standardized features containing log-prices, squares, pairwise products, immediate payoff, cross-sectional min/max/mean, and payoff-relevant extrema. For each fold, select ridge lambda from {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1, 1, 10} by minimizing validation squared error near the exercise boundary, generate out-of-fold continuation predictions, and update that fold’s cash flows without leakage. After completing the backward pass, refit four bootstrap ridge models per date using the selected lambda. At prediction, use the median continuation across models plus a date-specific exercise buffer. Choose each buffer from empirical margin quantiles {-0.15, -0.10, -0.05, 0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15} times the payoff scale by maximizing cross-fitted mean discounted payoff, with a one-standard-error rule favoring the more conservative, later-exercise buffer. Save ensemble coefficients, normalizers, and buffers in model.npz. This remains comfortably within 30 seconds for 256 paths.
plan.mechanism: Replace the parent with a cross-fitted, payoff-aware ensemble LSMC policy. The parent’s nearly unregularized full-sample regression can produce unstable continuation estimates from only 256 paths and train decisions on their own fitted targets. Out-of-fold prediction, stronger shrinkage, and conservative aggregation should reduce boundary overfitting and improve independent-path discounted payoff.
